cli.wake_help.wake: Inspect scheduled wakes and the supervisor that fires them
cli.wake_help.status: whether a supervisor is installed, and what it would fire next
cli.wake_help.status_install: install the supervisor now rather than waiting for the next schedule
cli.wake_help.status_uninstall: remove the supervisor; scheduled wakes then fire only when a session is open
cli.wake_help.install: install or repair the supervisor now (restarts a stale or stopped one)
cli.wake_help.list: every scheduled wake on this machine, soonest first
cli.wake_help.create: schedule a wake for a session (installs the supervisor on demand)
cli.wake_help.create_when: when to fire: a duration ("in 2m", "45s") or a clock time ("at 09:30")
cli.wake_help.create_message: the self-prompt delivered when it fires (at most {max} characters)
cli.wake_help.create_every: repeat every DURATION after the first fire ("5m", "1h", "8h30m")
cli.wake_help.create_notify: notify on completion of the wake's turn (default quiet: scripted arms match the contract; errored turns notify regardless)
cli.wake_help.serve: run the supervisor in the foreground (what the LaunchAgent runs)
cli.wake_help.serve_once: fire whatever is due right now, then exit
